turns.text: Hey Lloyd, did you check if my package from Amazon arrived? I ordered a new mechanical keyboard.
I don't have access to your real-time shipping status, Alan. You might want to check your email or the Amazon app for the latest updates.
Ugh, fine. Anyway, I was looking at that MonoNav project for the drone class. It's pretty basic. It uses stereo cameras for depth estimation, which is kind of overkill for simple indoor avoidance.
Stereo cameras can indeed be computationally expensive. Do you think a simpler approach would work better for your use case?
Probably. I might try swapping the input module. But first, I need to finish this dinner prep. Do you have a good recipe for salmon?
A simple pan-seared salmon with asparagus is always a hit. Would you like the step-by-step instructions?
No, I've got it. Just help me find that keyboard tracking number if you can.
I can't access external tracking systems, Alan. I'd recommend checking your order history directly.
Lloyd, I found out MonoNav actually updated its core architecture recently. It's no longer using stereo cameras.
That's interesting. What did they switch to?
It claims to use monocular depth for drone collision avoidance now. Much lighter on the hardware.
Ah, so it's MonoNav is a MAV navigation demo from 2026 that claims to use monocular depth for drone collision avoidance. That is a significant change from your earlier note.
Yeah. I need to update the config file for my simulation environment to match this new input type.
Understood. Will you need help writing a script to modify the config?
Not yet. I'm just debugging a weird noise in my microphone first. Can you suggest a good audio interface?
For clean audio, brands like Focusrite or Audient are usually reliable. Do you need a specific number of channels?
Just one channel for now. Thanks.
You're welcome. Let me know if you need help with the MonoNav config later.
